text: SeattleOpenData provides lightweight R interface Seattle Open Data Portal. package allows users search, filter, download datasets Seattle Open Data Portal directly R without manually constructing API queries, handling JSON responses, performing type conversion. Designed students, educators, researchers, journalists, civic technologists, analysts, SeattleOpenData reduces technical overhead required begin working municipal Open Data preserving access underlying Socrata infrastructure.

title: A Lightweight Interface to Seattle Open Data APIs
text: package provides three primary functions: seattle_list_datasets() retrieves live catalog available Seattle Open Data datasets, including human-readable keys, Socrata UIDs, names, available metadata. seattle_pull_dataset() downloads cataloged datasets using either human-readable key Socrata UID, support filtering, ordering, date ranges, optional column-name cleaning, optional type coercion. seattle_any_dataset() downloads data directly valid Socrata JSON endpoint without requiring dataset appear package catalog. Datasets retrieved seattle_pull_dataset() support arguments including: limit filters date date_field order clean_names coerce_types functions return tibble outputs. Advanced users may also provide raw SoQL conditions argument. SoQL, Socrata Query Language, query syntax used Socrata-powered Open Data portals. Additional information available Socrata developer documentation.

title: Pull any Seattle Open Data dataset from a Socrata JSON endpoint — seattle_any_dataset
code: # Examples that hit the live Seattle Open Data API are guarded so CRAN # checks do not fail when the network is unavailable or slow. if (interactive() && curl::has_internet()) {   # Build a JSON endpoint from a Socrata UID   uid <- "jguv-t9rb"   endpoint <- paste0("https://data.seattle.gov/resource/", uid, ".json")    out <- try(seattle_any_dataset(endpoint, limit = 3), silent = TRUE)   if (!inherits(out, "try-error")) {     head(out)   } }

text: catalog `key` supplied, `seattle_pull_dataset()` first retrieves live Seattle Open Data catalog look corresponding Socrata `uid`, sends second request download dataset . Supplying `uid` directly stable avoids ambiguity, keys provided readability classroom-friendly workflows. Dataset keys generated dataset names using [janitor::make_clean_names()]. keys derived live catalog metadata, Socrata UIDs stable identifiers. `seattle_pull_dataset()` designed common catalog-based workflows. arbitrary Socrata JSON endpoints included package catalog, use [seattle_any_dataset()]. `filters` argument intended simple exact-match filtering. complex conditions, use `` argument raw SoQL syntax. title: Pull a Seattle Open Data dataset — seattle_pull_dataset
code: if (interactive() && curl::has_internet()) {   # Pull by human-readable key   seattle_pull_dataset("seattle_pet_licenses", limit = 3)    # Pull by Socrata UID   seattle_pull_dataset("jguv-t9rb", limit = 3)    # Filter to one value   seattle_pull_dataset(     "jguv-t9rb",     limit = 3,     filters = list(primary_breed = "Domestic Shorthair")   )    # Filter to multiple values   seattle_pull_dataset(     "jguv-t9rb",     limit = 10,     filters = list(primary_breed = c("Domestic Shorthair", "American Shorthair"))   )    # Date filtering   seattle_pull_dataset(     "jguv-t9rb",     from = "2023-01-01",     to = "2024-01-01",     date_field = "license_issue_date",     limit = 100   )    # Advanced filtering with raw SoQL   seattle_pull_dataset(     "jguv-t9rb",     where = "species = 'Dog' AND secondary_breed = 'Mix'",     order = "license_issue_date DESC",     limit = 100   ) }
